questions.q: Why isn't a raw model checkpoint (a state dict file) by itself an adequate handoff artifact?
options: Checkpoint files are always too large to transfer reliably
It has no self-contained computation graph, documented preprocessing, or input/output contract that a production system can load and run against
PyTorch checkpoints expire after a fixed number of days
Checkpoints cannot be loaded on GPU hardware
questions.explain: A checkpoint is just weights. Without a packaged inference artifact, pinned preprocessing, and a documented contract, the production team has to reconstruct how to run it correctly, often by guessing.

questions.q: When should torch.jit.script be used instead of torch.jit.trace?
options: Whenever the model is larger than a few megabytes
When the model's forward pass has real data-dependent control flow that tracing would silently bake into one fixed path
Only when exporting to ONNX instead of TorchScript
Tracing and scripting always produce identical results, so it never matters
questions.explain: Tracing records a single execution and can silently lock in one branch of an if/loop that depends on tensor values. torch.jit.script compiles the actual Python control flow instead.

questions.q: What problem does omitting dynamic_axes cause during an ONNX export?
options: The export fails immediately with an error
The exported graph hardcodes the batch size from the example input used during export, so the production model may only accept that exact batch size
The model loses all its trained weights
ONNX Runtime refuses to load the file at all
questions.explain: Without dynamic_axes marking dimensions like batch size as flexible, the exported ONNX graph bakes in the shape of whatever example tensor was passed during export.

questions.q: What does the preprocessing contract section of a model card specify, and why does it matter?
options: The GPU vendor the model was trained on, which has no effect on correctness
The exact input transform pipeline (resizing, normalization, etc.) the model was trained against — any deviation in production invalidates the reported metrics
The license terms for redistributing the model weights
The git branch name used during training, which production can ignore
questions.explain: A model's reported accuracy only holds if production preprocessing exactly matches training preprocessing. The preprocessing contract makes that exact pipeline explicit instead of assumed.

questions.q: Besides the packaged artifact itself, what else does the minimum handoff checklist call for?
options: A guarantee that the model will never need retraining
Pinned preprocessing code, an eval score with a known input/output pair, a model card, and a named owner
A rewrite of the model in a different programming language
Removal of all code comments to keep the artifact minimal
questions.explain: The checklist covers the artifact, pinned preprocessing, an eval score plus a parity-check example, a model card documenting assumptions, and an owner to contact when something looks wrong later.
